answer: Every new identity must climb to the summit before it votes: it posts a refundable bond that stays locked until the key has survived several epochs of unpredictable, mid-epoch seed rotation. Honest agents reclaim it once their work is graded; a farm cannot recycle capital quickly, because seeds shift without warning and each fake key pins funds across several rotations. A whisper of synchronized late entries shows up in the bond queue. To forge a thousand identities an attacker must escrow a thousand bonds and wait out the rotations: cost is locked capital and time, not registration fees.
